newsitem.title: FRANCE: SNCF asks bidders to refine telecom offers.
newsitem.headline: SNCF asks bidders to refine telecom offers.

text.p: French state railroads group SNCF has asked telecoms operators which have expressed an interest in running its telecom network to "refine" their bids, a source close to the talks said.
SNCF is in talks with four operators about the running of its private telecoms network as a so-called alternative infrastructure when the French industry is liberalised in 1998.
The network could be used by rivals to France Telecom.
Among the bidders is Generale des Eaux, which teamed up in CEGETEL with British Telecom Plc and Germany's Mannesmann.
Another declared bidder is Bouygues in association with Italy's STET and Veba.
SNCF has set up a subsidiary, Telecom Developement, to market the excess capacity on its telecom network and a final deal is expected before the end of the year.
The network of Telecom Developpement currently represents 8,000 km of fibre optic cable and the unit will increase this to 11,000 to 12,000 km in three or four years.
Sources said the SNCF unit could have annual sales of some six to seven billion francs in about five or six years.
